Question: Why NRI is not allowed to vote for Indian election?
Answer: It is a wrong belief/ An NRI is allowed to vote in an Indian election. An NRI is very much an Indian Citizen whose tax-residency status is outside India. The NRI still holds an Indian Passport and can vote in two ways: People confuse NRI with a PIO/OCI. Such a person is no longer an Indian Citizen having relinquished his/her citizenship. This person is of Indian origin and that allows him/her to apply for a PIO/OCI card that eliminates the need to apply for a Visa every time to visit India.

Question: Is there anyone who got a UK tourist visa with just 1 lakh in their bank account and is unemployed?
Answer: It is very very unlikely that anyone without a job and with hardly any bank balance (just ₹1 Lakh) will get a UK Visitor Visa. This case straightway signals a potential immigrant. “Without job” is not the worrying part - there are many retired people or those who take early retirement. The UK High Commission wants to see last six months of bank statements. One can submit statements for multiple banks. One can even submit copies of Bank FD certificates. Basically the consular Visa officer wants to ensure that you have enough fund to travel to UK, stay in the UK using own funds and then return back home. Every country’s visa issuing officer wants to ensure that you have enough ties and incentives to return back. This case above is a complete RED flag,
